items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the
utilization of a pressurized mixing and dispensing system and the sale of
prepared liquor drinks
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3364

SPONSOR: SCARCELLA-SPANTON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the
utilization of a pressurized mixing and dispensing system and the sale
of prepared liquor drinks

 
PURPOSE:

Allow for the sale of ready to drink cocktails

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Amends paragraph (b) of section 106 of the ABC law to allow for the
preparation and on premise consumption of alcohol beverages that are
dispensed and served via a pressurized draft system, with.

 
EXISTING LAW:

Section 106 of the Alcoholic Beverage Control law presently prohibits
the storage of alcoholic beverages in anything other than (1) the
original container or (2) drinks prepared and kept in dispensing
machines, having capacities of not less than a gallon, which continually
mix such drinks.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Alcoholic Beverage Control Law prohibits the storage and service of
pre-mixed drinks unless such drink is dispensed through a machine that
continually "agitates" the mixture. This limitation prevents newer tech-
nology that meets higher food safety and sanitation level.  Newer
systems have been developed that are recyclable, tamper proof, airtight
kegs. Liter bottles are safely added to the unit with mix to create
cocktails, which are then dispensed by a common pressurized draft
system. The benefits of these systems are:

*the pressure from CO2 or nitrogen prevents growth of aerobic bacteria,
while also allowing the drink to be constantly and consistently mixed;

*the produced mixes have the required preserving agents that onsite
produced beverages lack; and,

*the commercially produced beverages are refined to the level that they
are colloid homogenous mixtures that do not require agitation, further-
ing the consistency of the mixed product.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2023 Session-New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
30 days after being signed into law

summary: Relates to the utilization of a pressurized mixing and dispensing system; permits a retail licensee for on-premises consumption to prepare and keep drinks containing alcoholic beverages in dispensing machines, having a capacity of not less than a gallon, utilizing a pressurized mixing and dispensing system.
